icons.source: scripts/extract_card_icons.py, harvested from the 54 card fronts already in public/cards/ -- nothing uploaded, nothing fetched. plantdex.online is proxy-blocked from this sandbox and did not need to be reached.
icons.how_labelled: Each front carries exactly two discs in two fixed slots, and herbs.json lists that card's two uses IN ORDER. Labels come from that cross-reference, not from somebody deciding what a picture means -- then every instance is re-classified against the medoids to check the ordering assumption actually holds.
icons.agreement: 85/90 use discs and 45/45 season tiles land on their own label. The five that do not all involve topical/bone/wound/energy, which are genuinely similar at the 48px grey resolution the check compares at. All twelve were then verified BY EYE against the rendered set and every label is correct: bone=joint, calm=seated figure, digestive=stomach, edible=fork and knife, energy=bolt, heart=heart with pulse, immune=shield, lungs=lungs, tea=steaming cup, topical=open hand, urinary=kidneys, wound=bandage.

review_flags.reason: All five faces supplied and complete. Validated by rendering PINE #41 from the template and comparing with the genuine card: every indicator glyph box matches exactly, and name, number, scientific name and encounter value sit on their measured baselines.

CambayDevanagari-Regular was named as a second card-number face and has not been supplied. It is absent from Pine #41, so I have no sample of it at all. The number renders in Baloo; if some printed cards set digits in Cambay, I cannot tell which.

Now Apigenin / Luteolin / Bisabolol / Chamazulene, each traced to c11 (Nutrients 2026 phytochemistry review) and c12 (Plant Cell Reports 2026). These are the characteristic constituents of German chamomile. The Greek alpha is dropped on the ARTWORK only -- Avenir-Medium has no alpha and a .notdef box is worse than the common name -- and 'alpha-bisabolol' is kept in full in the claims. 'Bisabolol' is the accepted common name of the compound, so this is a shortening, not a different substance.

Still no source. Searching the corpus for taste/bitter/sweet returns nothing for this species; one review mentions a 'sensory profile' without describing it. A taste note is an observation by somebody holding the plant.
The same. 'aroma'/'odour'/'scent' hits in the corpus are about other species or about extraction method, not about how chamomile smells.

c3 records chamomile as the most frequently cited species for EYE complaints in Mexican ethnomedicinal records. It is sourced, and it is deliberately NOT printed: a trait line reading 'Eye complaints' on a card people take outdoors reads as an instruction to put a plant infusion in an eye. Your call, and the claim is kept either way.

Still empty, and deliberately. The evidence pipeline searches EuropePMC, which is a biomedical corpus: across 41 retrieved sources there is nothing about how this plant grows. The only 'temperature' hit is a supercritical-extraction parameter and the only 'semi-arid' hit says where a sample was collected, not what the species requires. docs/environmental-indicators.md proposes Ellenberg L/F/T via BiolFlor as the source and gives the banding onto the deck's five slots; the retrieval has to run in Actions and has not run.
All four icons exist and the slot is ready. Eight CC0 observations spanning April-September across five countries is a sample of where people photographed it, not phenology.

RARITY IS A GAMEPLAY RATING AND IS NOT CONSERVATION STATUS. The two must not be wired together: GBIF reports this species as IUCN NOT_EVALUATED, and the retrieval already marks it `promotable: false` for that reason -- that is a statement about collecting pressure, not about how often a player meets the plant. The card renders the PROVISIONAL value 'Common' from `encounter_rate_provisional` so the slot's styling can be judged; the sourced `encounter_rate` is still null and the gameplay criteria are still unapproved.

Artwork follows the deck: all 45 printed fronts capitalise the specific epithet ('Taraxacum Officinale'), so deck_binomial() title-cases it for the RENDER only. The stored scientific_name, species_key, accepted_name and every claim keep the botanically correct 'Matricaria chamomilla'. Artwork styling and taxonomy are separate fields and neither is derived from the other.

render.proof: cardbase.pdf vs the unflattened Pine #41 PDF at identical geometry: 83% of pixels identical, and every differing pixel is per-card content.

typography.status: complete -- all five faces supplied by the owner, zero blocked strings
typography.sizes: CALIBRATED, not converted. The PDF's point sizes do not survive the layout's text transform (14.1pt x 800/234 gives 48px and renders two thirds of the true width). Each size reproduces the span's own measured width to within a pixel: Pine 127, Pinus spp. 238, 41 -> 52, # -> 28, Rare -> 84.
typography.baselines: the PDF's `origin` values, which are exact
typography.layers: three tones per string, all on ONE baseline: dark as an OUTLINE (not an offset shadow), the body colour, and a lighter highlight riding 2px high. Colours read from the PDF rather than eyedropped off a render.
typography.overflow: the whole composed stack -- outline, body and highlight together -- is scaled ~7% a step until it clears the next element. Stepping the FONT SIZE instead would shrink the letterforms while leaving the highlight offset and outline weight fixed, thickening the bevel as a name got longer.

calibration.method: closed loop against ALL 45 shipped cards: each candidate (size, stretch, stroke) is rendered through this renderer and measured against the genuine card under ONE identical colour mask, so target and output share a measurement space
calibration.common: size 68, stretch 1.00, stroke 3 -- 24 cards, mean height error 1.5px
calibration.scientific: size 47, stretch 1.30, stroke 0 -- 19 cards, mean height error 1.8px
calibration.superseded: every earlier number was fitted to Pine #41 ALONE. 'Pinus spp.' is ten characters with almost no ascenders, so its ink box is unrepresentatively short; matching it forced the sizes up and the shapes narrow at the same time, which is exactly the 'too large' + 'squashed' pair reported.
calibration.rarity_tiers: each tier has its OWN ink, which one card could not show: Common dark teal, Uncommon mauve, Rare pink, Epic blue. Pine is Rare, so calibrating from it gave every tier Rare's pink.
